problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2{v}^{2} \\ u-v\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-reversing?

examples.knowledge_point: Finding Regions Where a Transformation is Orientation-Preserving or Reversing
examples.problem:
Sketch the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $\mathbf{T},$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14043620/assets/0e620d5ca71a48c87a0d5942ffa8378964f6172bff7396c290024a5299531204.png)
is (locally) orientation-reversing.
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing at the points where the Jacobian determinant is negative:

$$
\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)}  <    0
$$

We have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14043620/assets/e947cb962ec1c0405292be18c838205b7be95ab083e07925d797b87e9c5b8654.png)

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}{e}^{v} & u{e}^{v} \\ 2u & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{v}\cdot (-2v)-u{e}^{v}\cdot 2u \\  & =-2{e}^{v}({u}^{2}+v).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{v}({u}^{2}+v) & <0 \\ {u}^{2}+v & >0 \\ v & >-{u}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=-u^2
$$

defines a downward-opening parabola, and the coordinates of, say, $(1,1)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing must be the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14043620/assets/2b6128c5a1737e3ad1fd82f91f5ccd320421ad3472ae8152440034ecea10d364.png)

feedback.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(2,4)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}\frac{{u}^{2}}{v} \\ uv\end{aligned}]?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{2u}{v} & -\frac{{u}^{2}}{{v}^{2}} \\ v & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{2u}{v}\cdot u-v\cdot (-\frac{{u}^{2}}{{v}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2{u}^{2}}{v}+\frac{{u}^{2}}{v} \\  & =\frac{3{u}^{2}}{v} \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(2,4)} & =(\frac{3{u}^{2}}{v})\,{|}_{u=2\,v=4} \\  & =\frac{3(2)^{2}}{4} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|3|\cdot \delta A \\  & =3\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
